subject: Pre-prod stress validation readout and rollout plan
messages:
From: Dylan Brooks <dylan.brooks@redwood.com>
To: Alex Rivera <alex.rivera@cariotech.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>, Dev Patel <dev.patel@redwood.com>
Date: 2027-03-27T09:12:00-07:00
Subject: Pre-prod stress validation: plan and quick questions

Alex —

Thanks again for running the pre-prod window this morning. Attached is the updated load plan (preprod-loadplan-v2.xlsx) we used for the runs and the raw log from the primary stress run (stress-run-20270327.log). High-level notes:

- We targeted 1.2k sustained qps (synthetic driver) with 95th percentile latency target of <= 450ms on the /generate route.
- We used the same prompt set you shared; KV cache warm-up was included for the last 15 minutes of the run.
- We observed transient token contention around the 34-minute mark (see stress-run-20270327.log lines 412-439).

Quick questions before we synthesize the results and hand this off to implementation:
1) Can you confirm the peak client concurrency you expect in production (we had estimates between 900–1,400 concurrent sessions)?
2) Were any custom reranking calls or third-party image attachments used in your end-to-end script we should account for?

Next steps I propose: we compile a short readout, assign a canary rollout window, and hand over an ops checklist to your SRE. Marissa, Dev — can you take a look at the attached playbook draft for the canary steps and call out anything missing?

Thanks,

Dylan
Customer Success Engineer
Redwood Inference

---
Attachments: preprod-loadplan-v2.xlsx (spreadsheet), stress-run-20270327.log (text log)

From: Alex Rivera <alex.rivera@cariotech.com>
To: Dylan Brooks <dylan.brooks@redwood.com>
Cc: ops@cariotech.com
Date: 2027-03-27T11:03:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Pre-prod stress validation: plan and quick questions

Dylan —

Appreciate the quick turnaround and the artifacts. A few clarifications from our end:

- Confirming target production concurrency is ~1,100 concurrent sessions during peak for the first month; we expect to scale to ~1,600 over Q3.
- No reranking calls in the current pipeline; there are periodic image attachments but those are stored in our CDN and not proxied through Redwood.

We reviewed the log; the transient spike you called out correlates with a client-side retry storm when our session router dropped a small fraction of keepalives. Our SRE will run a 2-hour extended replay tonight (scheduling window 23:00–01:00 PST).

Please include an explicit rollback trigger in the playbook: if 95p latency increases by >30% for 10 minutes OR error rate >1% sustained for 5 minutes, we should abort. Also add a capacity floor check so we don't exceed your dedicated pool limits.

I'll be on the call for the readout tomorrow morning.

—Alex
Head of Platform Ops, Cariotech
alex.rivera@cariotech.com

From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>

Date: 2027-03-27T13:08:00-07:00
Subject: RE: Pre-prod stress validation: plan and quick questions

All —

Thanks for the logs, Alex. I pulled the parsed metrics into the summary doc at the Drive link (see related_links). Key changes I've made to the playbook (attached canary-rollout-playbook.md):

- Canary window: 04/02 02:00–06:00 UTC. We'll run two 30-minute gradual ramps: 25% baseline, then 75% target.
- Acceptance checks: 95p latency <= 450ms, p50 <= 120ms, token cost variance within +8% of baseline.
- Rollback triggers: match Alex's ask + add retry budget crossing 20% over baseline for 10 minutes.
- Capacity safety: auto-fallback to smaller model variant if queue depth > 200 for more than 2 minutes (Dev to confirm variant mapping).

Dev — please confirm the model fallback mapping and whether the runtime can perform the variant swap within 45s. Grace — can you own the public-facing readout and schedule the executive handoff next week with Cariotech?

Marissa
Onboarding Lead, Redwood Inference
---
Attachments: canary-rollout-playbook.md (markdown)

From: Dev Patel <dev.patel@redwood.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>, Dylan Brooks <dylan.brooks@redwood.com>, Grace O'Connor <grace.oconnor@redwood.com>
Cc: Alex Rivera <alex.rivera@cariotech.com>
Date: 2027-03-27T16:41:00-07:00
Subject: Re: RE: Pre-prod stress validation: plan and quick questions

Marissa —

Confirming runtime behavior: we can perform a model variant swap (full weight switch) in ~30–40s under current infra. The safe fallback variant is "rw-medium-8q" and preserves most latency characteristics; token cost expected to rise ~3%. I'll add the exact mapping and a small operator script to the playbook (temporary: scripts/fallback-swap.sh).

I'll also set an autoscale cushion for the canary to hold an extra 10% headroom to avoid hitting reserved pool limits.

Dev
Senior Runtime Engineer, Redwood Inference

Deliverables ahead of the call (owners):
- Public readout slide deck (Grace) — link will be shared 1 hour before the meeting.
- Finalized canary playbook (Marissa/Dev) — I'll check the Drive link after you post the updated script.
- Post-canary reporting template (Dylan) — include the exact metrics, 95/50 latencies, cost deltas, and top three observed anomalies.

If the replay tonight surfaces any other abnormalities, please flag in the shared Drive and I'll triage. Otherwise see you on the 29th.

Regards,
Grace O'Connor
